transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Gotcha, so from your side it feels like the front desk has things covered.  

When she's at lunch or on another call, what happens to the calls that come in then?
User: We just call people back when we can. It's worked for us so far.
Agent: Yeah, makes sense — a lot of offices run it that way.  

When you do call back, how often do you find they’ve already booked somewhere else or just don’t pick up anymore?
User: We never really counted misses. Honestly, it doesn't seem to be a big issue for us.
Agent: Totally hear you — if it hasn’t felt painful, it’s not going to be top of mind.  

Out of curiosity, are there any times you *do* wish you had a bit more control on the phones — like after-hours, lunches, or when it gets really busy?
User: We manage as it comes. Janet's been here 9 years, she knows how to handle it.
Agent: Totally get that — having a “Janet” who just handles it is gold.  

So if Janet is out sick or on vacation, what usually happens with the phones then?
User: We manage with whoever's available. It's not ideal, but we get by without much trouble.
Agent: Got it, so it’s a bit patchwork at times, but it doesn’t feel painful enough to overhaul anything.  

If you *could* improve just one thing about how calls are handled today, what would you change first?
User: Honestly, just making sure we don't miss those calls during busy times might be the only thing.
Agent: Got it—that helps, thanks for being straight about it.  

When you hit those really busy stretches, how does it usually play out—do calls go to voicemail, get put on hold, or just ring out until someone can grab them?
User: They usually go to voicemail or just ring until someone can pick up. We try to get back soon.
Agent: Gotcha, so some hit voicemail and some just ring until someone’s free, then you return them when you can.  

When those go to voicemail, do most people actually leave a message, or do you think a chunk of them just hang up and move on?
User: Some leave messages, but I guess a few might hang up. Not sure how many, really.
Agent: Yeah, that’s usually what we see — the quiet ones who hang up are the ones that slip through.  

If one of those hang‑ups is worth, say, a few hundred or a few thousand dollars to you, would it *hypothetically* be interesting to have something that answers right away, books them in, and sends you the details, instead of hoping they leave a voicemail?
User: Sounds like a solution looking for a problem. We don't have too many hang-ups, as far as I know.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — if it feels like a “nice‑to‑have,” it’s not worth disrupting what’s working.  

Just so I don’t chase something you don’t need, are you mainly trying to keep things exactly as they are, or are you at least open to hearing what it *would* look like if those busy-time calls were fully covered, just to compare?
User: I'm open to hearing more, but Janet's system works well. How would this really change things?
Agent: Makes sense — and I’m not here to replace Janet, more to back her up.  

So if we zoom in on those busy stretches where calls hit voicemail or ring a while, would it help if, in those moments only, every caller was answered right away, screened, and either booked or messaged to Janet with exactly what they need?
User: Alright, as a backup layer, I can see it. Book your demo. Give me a call at +16175550005.
Agent: Got it, that’s helpful — and I like how you’re thinking of this as a backup for Janet, not a replacement.  

Quick thing: do you prefer we walk through this in a short 20–25 minute demo, or would you rather a tighter 10–15 minute overview just to see if it’s worth going deeper?
User: Let's do the 10–15 minute overview first. I want to see if it's worth diving deeper.
Agent: Gotcha, that’s totally fair — we can keep it tight and to the point.  

When’s usually better for you for a quick overview with Jay — earlier in the day or later in the afternoon?
User: Earlier in the day works best for me. Let's aim for a morning slot if possible.
Agent: Got it, mornings are best.  

What does your schedule look like tomorrow morning between, say, 9 and 11 your time?
User: Tomorrow at 10 AM works for me. Let's go ahead and schedule it then.
Agent: Perfect, tomorrow at 10 AM works.  

And just so Jay can tailor it properly, what type of business are you running there?
User: We run an auto body shop here in Boston. Focus on repairs, paint jobs, and collision work.
Agent: Nice, that helps — auto body in Boston, collision and paint is a perfect fit for this.  

For tomorrow at 10, do you prefer we call that number you shared ending in 0005, or is there a direct line you want Jay to use for the overview?
User: The number ending in 0005 works fine. I'll be expecting the call tomorrow at 10.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll have Jay give you a call tomorrow at 10 on the 0005 number for a tight 20‑minute overview, no commitment—he’ll walk you through how this can back up Janet during those busy times and after-hours, and you can decide if it’s worth going deeper. Thanks for making the time today, I’m looking forward to hearing how it lands for you—have a great rest of your day!
